processing.note: Optional note

ironwood_totems.name: Ironwood Totems

processing.note: Höggva: We hew the oak log down to three identical cubes using axe, measuring by eye and hand-span.
Soft seal protects corners from chipping, safe for small hands

assembly.note: Dip each block in warm resin_seal, wipe excess. The seal soaks into end-grain, hardens to a satin finish. Stack to dry—they'll click together with satisfying weight.

ironwood_totems.flavor_text: Every fortress begins with a single stone. A child who masters these blocks learns the first law of creation: what stands must first be stacked.

final_visual.The Blocks: 3 identically-sized oak cubes, honey-gold with visible grain. Corners slightly softened by the resin coating.
final_visual.The Finish: Satin sheen from resin_seal—not glossy, not matte. Warm to the touch.
final_visual.The Weight: Satisfyingly heavy. These are serious blocks.

sun_wheel_chaser.name: Sun-Wheel Chaser (Sólhjól)

processing.note: Höggva: Split and square the ash log in one action. The grain must run continuous—a sawn rod will snap under bending, but a hewn billet will yield to the sun's curve.
Boil the rod in water until the lignin softens. We seethe the wood until it yields like wet leather in the hands.
Sveigja: Pin the hot rod into a circular frame while steam still rises. Force it into its 'memory' before it cools.
Sníða: Carve the birch to a squared grip that won't slip in a frozen mitten, leaving the natural Y-fork at the tip to cradle the hoop.

assembly.note: Carve a scarf joint where the hoop ends meet so the circle remains flush. Bind with wet sinew—as it dries, it shrinks and bites into the ash with a serpent's grip. The guide_stick stays separate.

sun_wheel_chaser.flavor_text: The Sun-Wheel is the ghost of the summer sun. By chasing it across the winter rime, the children keep the path warm for the light's return in the spring.

final_visual.The Hoop: Golden-grey ash, bound in a perfect circle with a seamless scarf joint and dark sinew wraps.
final_visual.The Stick: Silver birch with a squared handle and a bone-white Y-fork at the tip.
final_visual.The Motion: Balanced and swift, leaping over roots and stones as if it has a spirit of its own.
final_visual.The Sound: A soft rumble on packed snow, a clatter on frozen earth.
final_visual.The Scent: The smell of boiled wood, forest resin, and the salt of dried sinew.

yule_wreath.name: Yule Wreath

processing.note: Flétta: Braid three green birch wands together while the sap is alive. A single bent branch is weak, but a trinity of braided birch creates a circle that will never lose its heart.

assembly.note: Bind the braid's ends with sinew to close the circle. Tuck pine_needles into the plait for greenery. Use pine_resin as the Forest's Glue to seat the rowan_berries—the blood of the earth in the snow.

yule_wreath.flavor_text: The wreath is a physical manifestation of the Endless Cycle. It signals the Gift-Bringer will once again fulfill the Compact, a wheel of hope until the light returns.

final_visual.The Base: Three intertwined birch branches forming an 8-inch ring. The pale bark shows through the greenery.
final_visual.The Greenery: Pine needles tucked throughout, still fragrant. Birch bark curls add white contrast.
final_visual.The Berries: Clusters of rowan berries—bright red against the green and white, held fast by amber resin.
final_visual.The Scent: Pine and birch, with the sweet sticky note of fresh resin.
final_visual.Hanging: A loop of sinew at the top for the door.

north_wind_whirler.name: North-Wind Whirler

processing.note: Höggva: Hew the dense maple log into a rough octagonal blank on the Höggvabekkr. The mass is there—the body shape with its stem socket waiting to be turned.
Renna: Shape the spinning blank on the pole lathe (Rennubekkr) at the Snikkarabekkr. Wide at equator, tapered to needle-point, with the stem socket carved at crown.
Hvíta: Submerge the wood in the Ketill to bleach it white. We use the action of Sjóða (seething) to drive the milk into the grain.
Blanda: Mix the resin and fat over the fire to create a hard-wearing guard for the wood.

assembly.note: Dip the spin-tip in the warm seal. The amber resin against the bleached white body is the mark of a master Snikkari.

north_wind_whirler.flavor_text: When the whirler hums, the winter spirits are listening. Children race these across frozen lakes to see whose can outrun the setting sun.

final_visual.The Body: Dense maple (Hlynr), widest at the equator. Brilliant white like a frost-giant's tooth.
final_visual.The Stem: Integrated handle carved directly from the heartwood for a palm-launch.
final_visual.The Tip: A dark, glass-like amber point that bites into the ice.
final_visual.The Motion: A white blur that hums as it sleeps.
final_visual.The Scent: Cold milk, maple sap, and the sting of pine pitch.

aurora_callers.name: Aurora Callers

processing.note: Höggva: Hew the pine log into blocky rough-outs—one mother swan shape, three cygnet masses. The skíð still holds the bark but shows the forms waiting within.
Sníða: On the shaving horse, pull the drawknife to release the graceful curves. The mother's arched neck, the cygnets' teardrop bodies—pine yields easily to the blade.
Hvíta: Submerge the carved swans in lye and milk. The alkaline solution bleaches pine to frost-white while milk proteins soften the grain for a matte finish.
Final waterproof coat for bath use

assembly.note: Brush warm resin_seal over the bleached swan family. The seal locks in the frost-white finish and waterproofs the toys for bath play. The cygnets nest against the mother's flanks.

aurora_callers.flavor_text: Legend says the Northern Lights were born from swans trapped in the ice—their frantic wings painting the shimmering sky. These frost-white bath toys represent the trapped swans.

final_visual.Mother Swan: Graceful arched neck, wings folded. Pure frost-white from the lye-milk soak with a subtle amber sheen from the resin seal.
final_visual.The Cygnets: Three small teardrop shapes with upturned heads. They bob around the mother in the water.
final_visual.The Finish: Matte white under glossy seal. Waterproof—these are bath toys.
final_visual.In Water: They float upright, the pine's natural buoyancy keeping them stable. Push one down and it pops back up.
final_visual.The Scent: Pine and resin—the forest captured in the bath.

frost_voice_chime.name: Frost-Voice Chime

processing.note: Birch is a resonant tonewood; five bars carved to graduated lengths, notched underneath to tune each pitch
Pine rived into a shallow trough—the hollow amplifies and warms the tone
Thin coating seals the bars without dampening vibration

assembly.note: Lay birch_bark strips across the sound_box as cushioning rails—this lets bars ring freely. Rest tuned_bars across the rails, spacing evenly. Loop sinew loosely through each bar's center notch to keep them in place without binding. Rub lye_soap lightly over the bars' striking surfaces. A small birch stick serves as the mallet.

frost_voice_chime.flavor_text: The sound of cracking ice, captured in wood. The children play songs that keep the darkness at bay, each note rings with defiance against the longest night.

final_visual.The Bars: Five birch bars, pale and smooth, arranged shortest to longest. Each has a subtle notch underneath where the pitch was tuned.
final_visual.The Box: Pine sound box, open-topped trough. The grain runs lengthwise to direct the sound upward.
final_visual.The Rails: Birch bark strips cushion the bars, letting them vibrate freely.
final_visual.The Mallet: A simple birch stick, included. Rounded tip for a soft strike.
final_visual.The Sound: Clear, bell-like tones. The pentatonic scale—no wrong notes, only winter songs.

light_bringer_candle.name: Light-Bringer Candle

processing.note: Höggva: On the Höggvabekkr, rive the oak to find the straight heart-grain and hew it into a heavy, squared block. This ensures the base will never crack from the candle's heat.
Sníða: At the Snikkarabekkr, carve the deep socket to hold the tallow and a wide, steady foot. Etch a shallow groove at the base to cradle the vow-scroll.
Sníða: Carefully peel the inner bast fibers from the birch. Twist these into a tight cord and press them on the bench; this organic line drinks the fat better than any sinew.
Grafning: Score the ancient vow into the silver skin of the Björk: 'At the darkest time, bring light.' The bark preserves the oath even as the candle burns.
Mala: Grind the blue berries in the Mylna to a fine powder. This dust purifies the hall and fills the air with the scent of the high mountains.
Sjóða: Seethe the tallow in the Ketill and fold in the juniper dust. The heat marries the mountain scent to the fat, creating a slow-burning incense.

assembly.note: Blanda: Suspend the birch wick in the oak socket and pour the fat in slow watches. Press pine needles into the soft top for forest scent. Tuck the vow into the oak's base. Read aloud before lighting.

light_bringer_candle.flavor_text: At the darkest time, bring light. At the coldest time, bring warmth. At the hungriest time, bring gifts. A beacon of juniper and heart-oak to guide the Gift-Bringer through the January rime.

final_visual.The Pedestal: Heavy, dark Oak with a hand-carved soul. It sits with the weight of tradition.
final_visual.The Candle: A cream-colored pillar of tallow, textured with green needles like spears in the snow.
final_visual.The Wick: A twisted birch-bast cord that burns with a tall, steady, and clean golden flame.
final_visual.The Scent: Sharp juniper, fresh pine, and the deep, earthy honey-smell of rendered tallow.
final_visual.The Ritual: As the flame melts the fat, the room is cleansed. The birch scroll at the base reminds all that the cycle of light always returns.

nisse_offering_basket.name: Nisse Offering Basket

processing.note: Rowan berries grind to a warm orange powder—the Nisse's favorite color
Cheerful orange soap, fragrant and festive. A small luxury.
Falda ok Sauma: Soften bark by hearth, fold into box, pierce corners with bone awl, stitch with wet sinew. As sinew dries, basket becomes drum-tight.

assembly.note: Line the basket bottom with pine_needles for cushioning and scent. Nestle the orange_soap bar in the center. Scatter lingonberries around it—bright red against the white bark. The basket is ready to leave by the hearth on the longest night.

nisse_offering_basket.flavor_text: Children learn to leave a basket to the household Nisse each winter. The old bargain is simple: small gifts ensure small blessings. Neglect breeds mischief.

final_visual.The Basket: Small birch bark container, about palm-sized. White bark with visible lenticels, corners neatly stitched.
final_visual.The Soap: Orange bar nestled in pine needles. Carved with a simple Nisse face or rune.
final_visual.The Berries: Lingonberries scattered like rubies around the soap.
final_visual.The Bedding: Pine needles line the bottom—green against white bark.
final_visual.The Scent: Pine, rowan, and the clean sharp smell of lye soap.
final_visual.The Tradition: Left by the hearth on Yule Eve. Gone by morning, if the Nisse is pleased.

grand_lineage_chess_set.name: Grand-Lineage Chess Set

processing.note: Höggva: On the Höggvabekkr, hew the logs into long, squared-off bars. It is far easier to turn a square than a round log, and removing the bark protects the lathe-cord from grit.
Renna: On the Rennubekkr, spin the squared billets into the 32 pieces of the armies. We turn them in 'strings' (multiple pieces on one bar) before cutting them apart.
Höggva: Hew thin, flat planks from both woods. These must be planed perfectly flat to ensure the battlefield is level.
Þrýsta: Cut the planks into 64 squares and join them edge-to-edge. Use the Press method with wedges to lock the birch and oak into their checkered marriage.
Blanda: Seethe (Sjóða) the milk and ash into a thick kalk-white. This is the 'Armor of Light' for the birch army.
Blanda: Our amber Run-lakk. It binds the grain of the board so it does not pull apart when the hall grows dry in winter.

assembly.note: Whitewash the birch army (Hvíta-her). Seal the entire battlefield and all warriors in warm resin. The oak warriors (Myrkr-her) will glow like honey against the chalky white of their enemies.

grand_lineage_chess_set.flavor_text: Light against shadow, patience against cunning. A board for kings, carved by the hands of a master who respects the grain.

final_visual.The Board: A heavy checkered slab of birch and oak, encased in a thick oak frame. No gap can be felt between the squares.
final_visual.The Armies: 32 hand-turned pieces. The Birch is bone-white; the Oak is deep, textured brown. They 'clack' with authority when moved.
final_visual.The Finish: A rich, amber satin glow. It smells of the deep forest and the clean hearth.
final_visual.The Heirloom: This set will outlast your hall. It is wood made immortal by the joiner's skill.

wool_warden_effigy.name: Wool-Warden Effigy

processing.note: Hot water and agitation mat the fibers into thick, seamless felt—no edges to fray, no seams to split
Strong thread for stitching features and reinforcing stress points

assembly.note: Cut two body shapes from wool_felt—front and back. Stitch edges with wool_spool thread, leaving a gap. Stuff firmly with loose wool_fiber until the figure holds its shape. Close the gap. Add simple stitched features: two dots for eyes, a line for mouth. The face should be kind but watchful.

wool_warden_effigy.flavor_text: A small guardian for small sleepers. Place it in the cradle and the winter spirits will pass by. Generations of children have clutched these through fever and nightmare alike.

final_visual.The Shape: Simple humanoid form, about 6 inches tall. Round head, stubby arms, no legs—a swaddled figure.
final_visual.The Material: Cream-colored wool felt, soft but dense. Visible fiber texture.
final_visual.The Face: Two dark stitched dots for eyes, a gentle curved line for mouth. Watching, not staring.
final_visual.The Stuffing: Firmly packed wool_fiber inside—squeezable but holds its shape.
final_visual.The Feel: Warm even when cold. Soft enough for a sleeping child's grip.
final_visual.The Wear: Meant to be loved hard. Edges soften with use, not unravel.

great_bear_sentry.name: Great-Bear Sentry

processing.note: Strong thread for seams that must survive years of hugging
Dense plain-weave fabric—sturdy shell that won't tear or pill

assembly.note: Cut bear pattern from wool_fabric: body (×2), head (×2), ears (×4), arms (×4), legs (×4). Stitch pieces inside-out, then flip. Stuff each limb with wool_fiber before attaching to body. Stuff body and head firmly. Attach head last. Embroider simple eyes and nose with dark wool_spool. Leave seams visible—this is honest craft, not factory perfection.

great_bear_sentry.flavor_text: Set him at the foot of the bed and nothing will disturb your sleep. The great bear watches through the night, soaking up bad dreams and breathing out warmth.

final_visual.The Shape: Classic teddy bear silhouette, about 10 inches seated. Round belly, stubby limbs, circular ears.
final_visual.The Fabric: Cream or grey wool_fabric with visible weave texture. Not plush—this is woven wool, sturdy and honest.
final_visual.The Face: Embroidered features: two small dark eyes, triangular nose, simple mouth line. Expression is calm, watchful.
final_visual.The Joints: Arms and legs are attached but not articulated—the bear sits naturally, stands with support.
final_visual.The Weight: Satisfyingly heavy from dense wool_fiber stuffing. A solid presence.

rune_singer_blocks.name: Rune-Singer Blocks

processing.note: Höggva: Hew oak log into identical cubes; each face ready for carving
Rowan orange—the color of firelight and protection
Vibrant tallow paint that soaks into carved grooves
Protective seal that hardens the painted runes

assembly.note: Carve a different Elder Futhark rune into each block face (6 faces × multiple blocks = full alphabet). Fill carved grooves with orange_tallow_raw—wipe excess, leaving paint only in the carved lines. Seal all surfaces with resin_seal. The orange runes glow against honey-gold oak. Children trace the shapes with fingers before they know the sounds.

rune_singer_blocks.flavor_text: Before a child can speak, they must learn to stack. Before they can read, they must learn the runes. These blocks carry the first marks—the shapes that bind thought to memory.

final_visual.The Blocks: Oak cubes, honey-gold with tight grain. Heavier than they look.
final_visual.The Runes: Each face carved with a single Elder Futhark rune. Orange paint fills the grooves—the symbols pop against the wood.
final_visual.The Set: 24 blocks for the full Elder Futhark, plus 6 blanks for building.
final_visual.The Finish: Resin seal gives a satin sheen. The runes are protected but tactile—small fingers trace them naturally.
final_visual.The Stack: These are building blocks first, alphabet second. Towers and walls, then words.
final_visual.The Sound: Solid oak clicks when stacked. Satisfying clatter when they fall.

borealis_birds.name: Borealis Birds

processing.note: Pine floats naturally; mother swan carved with graceful neck and hollow belly for stability
Three small cygnets—simple teardrop shapes that bob upright in water
Pure white base from birch ash
Opaque white base coat—the snow beneath the aurora
Warm orange from rowan—the fire curtains of the aurora
Aurora fire paint—applied in streaks over white
Cool blue from juniper—the shimmer between the flames
Aurora shimmer paint—blended into orange edges
Final waterproof coat for bath use

assembly.note: Base coat all bodies in white_tallow_raw—two coats for full opacity. While tacky, streak orange_tallow_raw across wings and backs in sweeping arcs. Blend blue_tallow_raw into the orange edges while wet, creating the aurora's characteristic color-dance. Let dry completely. Seal everything with resin_seal for waterproofing. The mother's wings get the most color; cygnets are mostly white with hints of color.

borealis_birds.flavor_text: The swans that escaped the ice carry the dancing sky on their feathers forever. White base, orange fire, blue shimmer—when children play with these in the bath, the aurora follows.

final_visual.Mother Swan: Graceful arched neck, wings suggested by carved ridges. White base with dramatic orange and blue aurora streaks across the back and wings.
final_visual.The Cygnets: Three small teardrops with upturned heads. Mostly white with subtle aurora hints—they haven't earned their full colors yet.
final_visual.The Colors: White snow-base, orange fire-streaks, blue shimmer at the edges. The aurora captured in paint.
final_visual.The Finish: Glossy from resin_seal. Waterproof and bath-ready.
final_visual.In Water: They float upright, pine's buoyancy keeping them stable. The colors dance on the water's surface.
final_visual.The Set: Mother and three cygnets. They cluster together naturally when floating.

rag_doll.name: Rag Doll

processing.note: Metal teeth comb retted flax; long line_flax for thread, short tow for stuffing
Fine linen thread—stronger than wool, smoother to the touch
Plain weave linen—cool, crisp, durable

assembly.note: Cut simple body shape from linen_fabric—head, torso, and limbs as one piece (×2). Stitch edges with linen_spool, leaving gap. Stuff with tow (the hackle byproduct) for authentic rag-doll softness. Close gap. Embroider simple face: two dots, curved smile. Hair is loose tow strands stitched to scalp. No fancy clothes—the linen itself is the beauty.

rag_doll.flavor_text: Woven from the first flax of summer, stuffed with the chaff of the harvest. She carries the warmth of the growing season into the frozen months.

final_visual.The Shape: Simple humanoid form, about 8 inches tall. Arms and legs extend from a single body piece—no separate limbs.
final_visual.The Fabric: Natural linen—pale cream with subtle texture. Cool to the touch.
final_visual.The Face: Two embroidered dots for eyes, a gentle curved smile. Simple and timeless.
final_visual.The Hair: Loose tow fibers stitched to the head—straw-gold, slightly wild.
final_visual.The Stuffing: Tow chaff inside—soft but with body. She bends but holds her shape.
final_visual.The Feel: Cool linen exterior, giving softness within. Lighter than wool dolls.

sun_whirler.name: Sun-Whirler

processing.note: Dense oak disc, about 4 inches diameter—the mass stores momentum
Long fibers separated for cord-making
Strong twisted cord that won't snap under spinning tension

assembly.note: Drill two holes near disc center. Thread linen_cord through both holes, tie ends to form a loop. Rub tallow into the cord holes to prevent wear. Press crushed rowan_berry into decorative grooves on the disc face—orange sun-rays against oak. To play: loop cord around fingers, wind the disc, pull hands apart rhythmically. The disc spins and hums.

sun_whirler.flavor_text: Pull the cord and the disc sings. The faster it spins, the louder it calls. Children spin these during the darkest days to remind the sky what warmth sounds like.

final_visual.The Disc: Heavy oak circle, 4 inches diameter. Decorative grooves radiate from center like sun rays, stained orange with rowan.
final_visual.The Cord: Natural linen loop, about 2 feet total. Twisted tight for strength.
final_visual.The Holes: Two small holes near center, tallow-smoothed to prevent cord wear.
final_visual.The Motion: Pull-release rhythm makes the disc spin and reverse. At speed, it blurs into a golden sun.
final_visual.The Sound: A rising hum that changes pitch with speed—the voice of the returning light.
final_visual.The Feel: Satisfying tension in the cord, gyroscopic pull from the spinning disc.

antler_clacker.name: Antler Clacker

processing.note: Natural forked tine trimmed to a handle with two arms—antler's dense structure amplifies sound
Flat bone discs with center holes—two pairs that clack against each other
Seals sinew knots to prevent unraveling

assembly.note: Thread sinew through each bone_disc pair, tie to the antler fork arms—two discs per arm, spaced to clack against each other. Dab resin_seal on all knots. When shaken, the disc pairs strike together, then strike the antler arms. The rhythm mimics galloping hooves.

antler_clacker.flavor_text: The clatter of bones on antler mimics the sound of reindeer hooves on frozen ground. Shake it during the longest night, and the Gift-Bringer's sleigh will always find your home.

final_visual.The Frame: Natural antler fork, cream-white with subtle grain. Handle is the main beam, two tines form the arms.
final_visual.The Discs: Four bone circles, slightly dished, strung in pairs. Polished smooth from handling.
final_visual.The Stringing: Sinew loops connect discs to antler arms, sealed with amber resin.
final_visual.The Sound: Sharp clatter of bone-on-bone, deeper thunk when discs hit antler. Rhythmic when shaken properly.
final_visual.The Motion: Grip handle, shake side-to-side. The discs swing and strike in syncopated rhythm.
final_visual.The Feel: Light but solid. The antler handle is warm and smooth.

fortunes_bones.name: Fortune's Bones

processing.note: Six bone cubes carved from dense leg bone—each face marked with runes 1-6
Hollowed birch cylinder, palm-sized—the dice rattle satisfyingly inside
Small bone pegs for tracking wagers and scores
Falda ok Sauma: Fold bark into drawstring pouch, stitch with sinew to keep the set together
Seals rune marks and protects bone surfaces

assembly.note: Carve rune numerals into each die face, fill marks with dark ash for visibility, seal with resin_seal. The cup's interior is left rough for good dice tumbling. Score_pegs store in small loops inside the pouch. Everything nests: dice in cup, cup and pegs in pouch. A complete game in a palm-sized package.

fortunes_bones.flavor_text: The Völva cast these to read the will of the gods. Children cast them to win each other's desserts. Shake the cup, spill the bones, and let fate decide.

final_visual.The Dice: Six bone cubes, cream-white with dark rune numerals. Slightly irregular—hand-carved, not factory-perfect.
final_visual.The Cup: Birch cylinder, open at top, palm-sized. Pale bark exterior, smooth interior.
final_visual.The Pegs: Ten small bone pins, pointed at one end. Used to track scores in soft wood or earth.
final_visual.The Pouch: Birch bark folded into a drawstring bag, sinew closure. Everything fits inside.
final_visual.The Sound: Sharp rattle of bone on wood when shaking. Satisfying clatter when dice spill.
final_visual.The Ritual: Shake the cup. Slam it down. Lift to reveal fate.

tale_weaver_set.name: Tale-Weaver's Set

processing.note: Ash flexes on impact—safe for play-fighting. Carved with fuller groove for authenticity.
Two birch halves hollowed to fit the blade
Sturdy leather for scabbard covering and belt
Belt loop and throat strap for the scabbard

assembly.note: Glue scabbard halves together with hide_glue, wrap in leather for a professional finish. Attach leather_hangers for belt carry. The blade should slide in and out smoothly with a satisfying 'shick.' Wrap the blade handle in leather strips, secured with sinew. The crossguard is carved integral to the blade—no metal needed.

tale_weaver_set.flavor_text: Every saga needs a hero, and every hero needs a blade. This set transforms the nursery into Valhalla, the woodpile into a dragon's hoard.

final_visual.The Blade: Pale ash sword, about 20 inches. Viking-style profile with gentle taper. Fuller groove carved down the flat. Rounded edges—safe but authentic.
final_visual.The Handle: Leather-wrapped grip, crossguard carved from the same ash blank. Pommel is a simple dome.
final_visual.The Scabbard: Birch core wrapped in brown leather. Brass-colored birch bark accent at throat.
final_visual.The Carry: Leather belt loop and strap. Hangs at the hip, saga-ready.
final_visual.The Draw: Smooth slide with a satisfying 'shick' as blade clears scabbard.
final_visual.The Weight: Light enough for a child, substantial enough to feel heroic.

jarl_shield_plaque.name: Jarl's Shield-Plaque

processing.note: Oak planks edge-joined into a round—authentic construction
Leather facing for the shield front
Gård-Lím: the binder that makes distemper paint
Deep blue from juniper
Blood red from lingonberry
Royal purple 'Rauðblár'—mixed blue and crimson in hide_glue binder
Protective topcoat

assembly.note: Stretch leather over shield_backing, secure at back with sinew lacing through drilled holes. Paint the leather face with purple_distemper—the velvety finish drinks the pigment. Add a simple rune or beast design in natural leather (masked before painting). Seal with resin_seal for protection. Attach sinew loop at back for wall hanging. This is display art, not a play shield.

jarl_shield_plaque.flavor_text: A wall-gift worthy of a chieftain's hall. The purple of 'Rauðblár' marks this as a treasure beyond price. Hang it with pride where the firelight can find it.

final_visual.The Shape: Round shield form, about 12 inches diameter. Oak backing, leather face.
final_visual.The Color: Deep royal purple—'Rauðblár'—velvety matte from the distemper. The color of kings.
final_visual.The Design: Simple rune or beast motif in natural leather, revealed by masking before painting.
final_visual.The Edge: Leather wraps around to the back, secured with visible sinew stitching.
final_visual.The Finish: Resin seal gives subtle sheen without destroying the velvety purple.
final_visual.The Hanging: Sinew loop at back. Meant to catch firelight on a dark winter wall.

wool_walker_bunny.name: Wool-Walker Bunny

processing.note: Strong thread for seams and jointing
Dense weave for durable shell
Internal anchors sewn into ear bases—allows ears to pose and hold position
Decorative nose button
Polished bone discs with carved pupils

assembly.note: Cut bunny pattern from wool_fabric: body (×2), ears (×4), arms (×4), legs (×4). Sew ear pieces around bone_toggles—this lets ears bend and hold poses. Stitch limbs, stuff with wool_fiber, attach to body. Stuff body firmly. Sew on bone_eyes, bone_button nose. Rub tallow into seams to soften and protect. The toggles inside make this bunny 'alive'—ears up, ears down, ears flopped to the side.

wool_walker_bunny.flavor_text: More than stuffing—there's a spirit in this one. Squeeze it through a hundred long nights and it only grows stronger, denser, more real.

final_visual.The Shape: Classic bunny form, about 10 inches tall. Long upright ears, round body, stubby limbs.
final_visual.The Ears: The signature feature—bone toggles inside let them pose. Stand them up, fold them down, flop them sideways.
final_visual.The Face: Polished bone eyes with carved pupils. Bone button nose. Embroidered whiskers and mouth.
final_visual.The Body: Cream or grey wool_fabric, firmly stuffed. Huggable but holds its shape.
final_visual.The Feel: Warm wool exterior, dense stuffing. The ears have satisfying resistance when posed.
final_visual.The Wear: Built for years of love. Seams are reinforced, tallow-treated for durability.

linen_lass.name: Linen Lass

processing.note: Line flax for thread, tow for stuffing—nothing wasted
Fine linen thread for seams and features
Crisp linen shell—cooler than wool
Sewn into shoulder joints—lets arms pose and hold
Decorative buttons for dress front
Polished bone with dark-stained pupils

assembly.note: Cut doll body and simple dress from linen_fabric. Sew arms with bone_toggles at shoulders—this allows posing. Stuff body and limbs with tow. Attach bone_eyes, embroider simple features. Dress is sewn integral to body, bone_buttons down the front. Hair is tow strands stitched to scalp, can be braided. Rub tallow into joints to keep them supple. She can wave, hug, or hold a child's hand.

linen_lass.flavor_text: She can wave, she can hug, she can hold your hand through the fever-dreams of winter sickness. Arms that move on their own, eyes that catch the firelight.

final_visual.The Shape: Classic rag doll form, about 12 inches. Round head, simple body, poseable arms.
final_visual.The Arms: Bone toggles at shoulders allow full rotation. She can wave, hug, or rest hands in her lap.
final_visual.The Face: Polished bone eyes catch firelight. Embroidered nose and smile. Warm expression.
final_visual.The Hair: Tow fiber stitched to scalp—straw gold, long enough to braid.
final_visual.The Dress: Simple linen shift, integral to body. Bone buttons down the front.
final_visual.The Feel: Cool linen exterior, soft tow stuffing. Arms move smoothly on their bone joints.

jingle_tambourine.name: Jingle Tambourine

processing.note: Ash ring with slots cut for jingles—flexible wood absorbs impact
Supple leather for drum head
Circular head stretched over frame
Hand grip on back
Jingle discs—paired in slots to clatter against each other

assembly.note: Stretch drum_skin over frame while wet—it shrinks tight as it dries. Lace edges with sinew through holes drilled in frame. Thread bone_button pairs on sinew through frame slots—they hang loose to jingle. Attach leather_strap to back as hand grip. The drum head can be struck or the whole instrument shaken for the jingles.

jingle_tambourine.flavor_text: The first instrument of celebration. Shake it and the bones rattle like laughter, like applause, like a hundred small welcomes.

final_visual.The Frame: Ash ring, about 8 inches diameter. Four slots hold paired bone jingles.
final_visual.The Head: Taut leather drum skin, pale and translucent. Responds to tap or slap.
final_visual.The Jingles: Four pairs of bone buttons on sinew—they clatter against each other and the frame when shaken.
final_visual.The Grip: Leather strap on back for secure one-handed hold.
final_visual.The Sound: Tap the head for a soft thump. Shake for bright bone-clatter. Combine both for rhythm.
final_visual.The Feel: Light and responsive. Natural to shake, slap, or tap.

solstice_storm_drum.name: Solstice Storm-Drum

processing.note: Thin birch board for bending into hoop
Sjóða: Boil the birch board until pliable—must work fast before it cools
Lye removes hair but keeps hide stiff—perfect for drum heads
Circular head larger than frame—shrinks tight when dried
Seals the hoop's scarf joint
Line flax for handle cord, tow for mallet padding
Sturdy cord for drum handle
Antler head wrapped in tow for soft strike

assembly.note: Bend supple_hoop into circle, overlap ends in scarf joint, seal with resin_seal. Stretch wet drum_skin over hoop, lace underneath with sinew through punched holes—it tightens as it dries. Cross linen_cord underneath as handle. Wrap mallet_head in tow padding, bind with sinew, attach to ash stick. Rub tallow into hide edge to prevent cracking. The finished drum is a frame drum—held by the cord, struck with the padded mallet.

solstice_storm_drum.flavor_text: Thunder in your hands. Strike it once and the storm answers. The Völva use drums like this to walk between worlds—but children just like the boom.

final_visual.The Frame: Birch hoop, about 14 inches diameter. Pale wood with visible grain.
final_visual.The Head: Raw hide stretched taut—translucent, amber-toned. You can see shadows through it.
final_visual.The Lacing: Sinew criss-crosses underneath, creating the signature pattern. Linen cord handle through the center.
final_visual.The Mallet: Antler head wrapped in tow padding on an ash stick. Produces a deep, resonant boom.
final_visual.The Sound: Deep thunder-boom that sustains and rolls. Strikes the chest as much as the ears.
final_visual.The Hold: Grip the cord handle, drum face outward. Strike and let the sound flow through you.

ash_hobbyhorse.name: Ash Hobbyhorse

processing.note: Stylized head with open mouth—ash is light but strong
Polished bone discs set into carved sockets
Bridle cheek pieces—functional decorations
Thread for mane attachment and saddle stitching
Colorful saddle blanket draped over stick
Bridle straps and reins
Bridle and reins

assembly.note: Drill socket in head base, friction-fit onto ash stick. Set bone_eyes into carved sockets. Attach leather_strap bridle with bone_button cheek pieces. Loop wool_fiber strands through drilled holes at crest for mane—the wilder the better. Drape wool_fabric saddle blanket over stick, tie with sinew. The second leather_strap becomes reins. Rub tallow into leather and wood joints. Ready to ride.

ash_hobbyhorse.flavor_text: The steed of imagination rides through kitchen and hall alike. Gallop it hard enough and you might just outrun the winter itself.

final_visual.The Head: Carved ash, stylized horse profile with open mouth. Light grey wood with visible grain.
final_visual.The Eyes: Polished bone discs set in sockets—they catch the light with life.
final_visual.The Mane: Shaggy wool_fiber loops along the crest—wild and flowing.
final_visual.The Bridle: Leather straps with bone button cheek pieces. Reins loop around for the rider's hands.
final_visual.The Stick: Ash pole, about 3 feet. Wool saddle blanket draped over it for grip.
final_visual.The Ride: Straddle the stick, grip the reins, and gallop. The head bobs with each stride.

frost_wyrm.name: Frost Wyrm

processing.note: Thread for construction and scale details
Body shell—dyed ice-blue
Belly scales and wing membranes
Internal spine—allows the body to pose and hold curves
Sharp fangs for the open maw
Wicked claws on vestigial legs
Glacier-blue painted over white bone
Ice-blue for scales and eyes
Dye for wool and leather

assembly.note: Dye wool_fabric ice-blue with blue_tallow_raw. Cut serpentine body pattern, sew with bone_toggles inside at intervals—this creates the poseable spine. Stuff with wool_fiber. Cut leather belly scales in overlapping strips, stitch underneath. Add leather wing stubs at shoulders. Set bone_teeth in open mouth, bone_eyes in sockets, bone_claws on small legs. The wyrm can coil, strike, or drape around a child's arm. About 24 inches fully extended.

frost_wyrm.flavor_text: The serpent of the frozen sky, coiled and waiting. Pose it to strike or curl it around your arm like a living thing. The old sagas say wyrms sleep beneath the glaciers.

final_visual.The Body: Serpentine form in ice-blue wool, about 24 inches long. Internal bone spine allows posing.
final_visual.The Scales: Overlapping leather strips on belly—natural brown against blue wool.
final_visual.The Head: Open maw with six bone fangs. Glacier-blue eyes. Menacing but huggable.
final_visual.The Wings: Vestigial leather wing stubs at shoulders—too small to fly, perfect for drama.
final_visual.The Claws: Four bone claws on small legs—positioned for gripping when wrapped around an arm.
final_visual.The Pose: Coil it, drape it, pose it to strike. The bone spine holds any position.

great_north_sleigh.name: Great North Sleigh

processing.note: Thin ash boards for runners—ash bends without breaking
Sjóða: Boil the ash board until pliable. ⏱ 30s timer—must bend before it cools
Curved at front to ride over snow—the classic sleigh profile
Heavy oak box frame for cargo—mortise-and-tenon joints
Thread for blanket attachment
Crimson blanket for the seat
Line flax for pull cord
Strong pull rope attached at front
Red for the frame—Gift-Bringer's color
Crimson paint for frame
Waterproof seal for runners
Decorative finials at front—the reindeer connection

assembly.note: Attach sleigh_frame to runners with mortise joints, reinforce with sinew lashing. Paint frame crimson with crimson_tallow_raw—let it soak into the oak. Seal runners with resin_seal for smooth glide. Set antler_finials at front corners as decorative posts. Dye wool_fabric crimson to match, drape as seat blanket. Attach linen_cord pull rope at front. Big enough for a doll passenger and a load of tiny gifts.

great_north_sleigh.flavor_text: Worthy of the Gift-Bringer himself. Load it with treasures and fly across the snow. This sleigh brings hope that no child will be forgotten, no hearth too distant to find.

final_visual.The Runners: Bent ash with classic upturned fronts. Sealed smooth for gliding.
final_visual.The Frame: Oak cargo box painted crimson—the Gift-Bringer's signature color.
final_visual.The Finials: Antler points at front corners—a nod to the reindeer team.
final_visual.The Blanket: Crimson wool draped over the seat. Warm and festive.
final_visual.The Rope: Linen pull cord at front for towing across the snow.
final_visual.The Scale: About 12 inches long—perfect for doll passengers and tiny gift loads.
final_visual.The Glide: Actually slides on smooth surfaces. Load it up and pull.

storm_wing_kite.name: Storm-Wing Kite

processing.note: Heavy thread for dense weave
Tight weave traps air—the sail that catches winter
Line flax for flight cord, tow for tail
High-tensile flight line—won't snap in strong winds
Rough twisted tail for stability

assembly.note: Lash birch sticks into cross frame with sinew. Stretch wool_fabric over frame, stitch edges. Apply hot smörring (pine_tar + tallow mixed) to the sail—it stiffens the wool into a rigid, wind-proof surface. Tie linen_cord bridle to frame cross-point. Attach tow_cord tail strips for stability. The treated sail is black from the tar, gleaming in wind.

storm_wing_kite.flavor_text: To fly the Storm-Wing is to feel the raw pulse of the winter sky. The woolen sail is treated with a hot smörring of pine_tar and tallow, petrifying the soft fabric into a rigid, wind-proof wing.

final_visual.The Frame: Crossed birch sticks, pale wood against dark sail. Classic diamond kite shape.
final_visual.The Sail: Wool fabric stiffened with pine_tar smörring—black and gleaming, rigid as leather.
final_visual.The Bridle: Linen cord meeting at the kite's center of lift. Strong enough for winter gales.
final_visual.The Tail: Tow cord strips trailing behind—shaggy and wild, stabilizing in turbulence.
final_visual.In Flight: The black diamond against grey winter sky. It pulls hard in wind, alive on the line.
final_visual.The Scent: Pine tar and sheep—the smell of Nordic winters.

puppet_theater.name: Puppet Theater

processing.note: Light pine for portable theater
Front frame with decorative arch—the stage window
Solid backdrop panel—hides the puppeteer
Thread for weaving the grand curtain
Wide fabric for the stage curtain
Blood-red for dramatic effect
Tallow dye bonds to wool's lanolin

assembly.note: Hinge proscenium_arch to stage_back with sinew loops—folds flat for storage. Dye wool_fabric crimson with crimson_tallow_raw. Hang curtain on birch stick rod across the top of the arch—it pulls aside for reveals. The back panel has a hand-hole for the puppeteer. Decorate the arch frame with carved knotwork. Table-top scale, about 18 inches tall.

puppet_theater.flavor_text: Every child is a Skald. This stage transforms the hearth-corner into Valhalla, Niflheim, or wherever the tale demands. The crimson curtain rises, and the old stories walk again.

final_visual.The Arch: Pine proscenium with carved knotwork. The stage window is about 12 inches wide.
final_visual.The Curtain: Crimson wool hanging from birch rod. Pulls aside dramatically for the show.
final_visual.The Back: Solid pine panel hides puppeteer hands. Cut-out at bottom for access.
final_visual.The Fold: Hinges flat for storage—takes up no more space than a book.
final_visual.The Scale: Table-top theater, about 18 inches tall. Perfect for finger puppets or stick figures.
final_visual.The Drama: Open curtain. Begin tale. The old stories live in the red-lit shadow.

stream_mill.name: Stream Mill

processing.note: Paddle wheel with carved vanes—catches stream current or hand cranking
Rotating grindstone with textured face
Stationary bone grinding surface—harder than wood
Hollowed oak block for stability and heft
Axle transfers paddle rotation to grinding disc
Falda ok Sauma: Fold bark into funnel shape, stitch seam with sinew to feed material to grinder
Waterproofs housing for stream placement

assembly.note: Set grind_plate in housing base. Mount grinder_mechanism above with axle through housing walls—the grind_disc should nearly touch the plate. Attach hopper_cone above the gap. Seal all joints with resin_seal for water use. Place in a stream with paddle wheel in current, or turn by hand. Drop berries in hopper, collect crushed pulp from the outlet. A working machine in miniature.

stream_mill.flavor_text: Drop a berry in the hopper, watch the wheels churn, and catch the juice of the forest. Learn a pattern of the cycle, the world is full of energy, if you know how to catch it.

final_visual.The Housing: Heavy oak block, hollowed inside. About 8 inches long, stable in stream current.
final_visual.The Wheel: Maple paddle wheel on one side—catches water flow or hand power.
final_visual.The Grinder: Maple disc spinning above bone plate. Narrow gap crushes whatever passes through.
final_visual.The Hopper: Birch bark cone funneling into the grinder gap from above.
final_visual.The Action: Water turns wheel, wheel turns grinder, hopper feeds berries, pulp exits below.
final_visual.The Lesson: Energy capture. Power transfer. The fundamental physics of the mill, toy-sized.

bergelmir_ark.name: Bergelmir's Ark

processing.note: Buoyant pine planks for hull sides
Heavy oak cradle provides ballast—the ark rights itself
Supple leather for the square sail
Casein preparation
Beina-mjólk binder for durable paint
Blood-red like Ymir's flood
Water-resistant crimson paint for the sail

assembly.note: Peg pine boards to oak keel, forming the classic coffin-boat shape (lúðr). Caulk all seams with hot pine_tar—the 'Black Blood' makes it watertight. Set mast in keel socket. Dye leather sail crimson with crimson_casein. Rig sail to mast with sinew lines. Rub tallow into hull exterior for smooth sailing. It actually floats and sails with the wind.

bergelmir_ark.flavor_text: A vessel of the Primordial Deluge. This ark mimics the lúðr that saved Bergelmir from the drowning blood of Ymir. Pine_tar—the Black Blood—caulks the seams to be 'blood-tight.'

final_visual.The Hull: Coffin-boat shape (lúðr)—pine sides on oak keel. Seams black with pine_tar caulking.
final_visual.The Keel: Heavy oak provides ballast. The ark self-rights when tipped.
final_visual.The Sail: Square leather sail dyed blood-crimson. Rigged Nordic style.
final_visual.The Tar: Black seams where pine_tar caulks the joints—the 'blood-tight' seal.
final_visual.In Water: It floats, it sails, it carries small figures through the deluge.
final_visual.The Myth: Bergelmir's escape vessel, when Ymir's blood drowned the world.

treasure_chest.name: Treasure Chest

processing.note: Heavy oak boards for a chest that lasts generations
Sealed box construction—no gaps, no peeking
Sawn horizontally after assembly—grain matches perfectly
Sturdy leather for hinges and closure
Two hinges at back, one closure strap at front
Line flax for lining thread
Fine thread for stitching lining
Soft linen to cushion treasures
Protective finish for the exterior

assembly.note: Attach leather_strap hinges at back with sinew stitching through drilled holes. Front strap becomes the closure—wraps around bone toggle or wooden peg. Line interior with linen_fabric, glued and stitched at edges. Seal exterior with resin_seal, buff with tallow. Carve owner's initials or rune into the lid. About 6 inches long—sized for a child's small treasures.

treasure_chest.flavor_text: Every child needs a place for secrets. Oak walls, leather hinges, and a linen bed for their most precious things. What goes inside is none of your business.

final_visual.The Box: Heavy oak chest, about 6 inches long. Grain matches between lid and body—proof of quality craft.
final_visual.The Hinges: Leather straps at back, stitched through wood. They flex but don't wear.
final_visual.The Closure: Front leather strap wraps around a bone toggle or wooden peg.
final_visual.The Interior: Soft linen lining cushions the treasures within.
final_visual.The Finish: Resin-sealed exterior gleams with amber warmth. Smooth to the touch.
final_visual.The Weight: Satisfyingly heavy. Oak doesn't make flimsy furniture.

yule_boar.name: Yule Boar

processing.note: Stocky oak body with bristled back ridge and proud snout
Curved tusks flanking the snout—Freyr's sacred beast
Small but fierce watchful eyes
Smooth maple wheels for rolling
Front and rear axles pinned to body
Pull strap leather
Loop for towing the boar to feast
Protective finish

assembly.note: Drill axle channels through boar belly. Mount axle_sets with sinew lashing for free rotation. Set bone tusks in drilled snout sockets, bone_eyes in face sockets. Attach pull_strap at neck with sinew loop. Seal entire body with resin_seal, buff with tallow for sheen. The boar rolls smoothly and pulls behind a walking child. About 10 inches long.

yule_boar.flavor_text: Freyr's sacred beast, rolling to the feast. In the old days, families swore oaths on the Yule Boar's back. This one carries smaller promises—but they still count.

final_visual.The Body: Stocky oak boar with carved bristle ridge along the back. Proud stance even on wheels.
final_visual.The Tusks: Curved bone tusks flanking the snout. The mark of Freyr's beast.
final_visual.The Eyes: Small fierce bone discs set in sockets. Watchful and wise.
final_visual.The Wheels: Four maple wheels on oak axles. The boar rolls smoothly after its owner.
final_visual.The Strap: Leather pull loop at neck. Drag the boar to the Yule feast.
final_visual.The Oath: In the old tradition, touch the boar's back when you make a promise. It still works.

nisse_boundary_levitator.name: Nisse Boundary Levitator

processing.note: Heavy oak for the cart's stability
Open-top cargo box—the rolling farmstead in miniature
Smooth maple wheels roll true
Maple drum on drive axle wraps the suspension line
Line flax for high-tensile cord, tow for friction wrap
Strong cord suspends the Nisse figure
Tow friction wrap on drum—wheels turn, drum turns, cord rises
Simple trailing axle
Vertical mast with pulley channel at top
Light birch guardian—small enough to levitate on thin cord
Weather sealer for outdoor patrol

assembly.note: Mount drive_axle at front, rear_axle at back. Set sentinel_pole upright in cart center, lashed with sinew. Thread linen_cord from cord_drum, up through pole channel, down to nisse_figure loop. As cart rolls forward, drum turns and winds cord—the Nisse rises. Pull back, he descends. Seal all exposed wood with resin_seal. The guardian never touches the ground.

nisse_boundary_levitator.flavor_text: A farmstead requires a watchful eye. Pull the cart and the Nisse levitates, patrolling the borders of your domain while never touching the ground.

final_visual.The Cart: Oak cargo box on four maple wheels. Heavy and stable, like a farm wagon.
final_visual.The Mast: Vertical oak pole rising from the cart center with cord channel at top.
final_visual.The Mechanism: Cord_drum on front axle—when wheels turn, drum winds the suspension cord.
final_visual.The Guardian: Light birch Nisse figure, arms outstretched, hanging from linen_cord.
final_visual.The Magic: Push the cart: Nisse rises. Pull back: Nisse descends. Always floating, never grounded.
final_visual.The Patrol: A child pulls the cart around the room's border. The Nisse watches over all.

dragon_scale_slicks.name: Dragon Scale Storm Slicks

processing.note: Three full hides—one each for jacket, hat, boots
Smoky black waterproof leather, supple and breathable
Four boards for frame, one for the press die
Taut frame holds wet leather flat during pressing
Diamond grooves carved deep—Nidhogg's scale pattern
Wet leather pressed hard; grooves become permanent scales
Toggle closures—two per garment piece

assembly.note: Cut dragon_scale_leather into pattern pieces. Stitch with sinew: jacket with overlapping front panels, rain hat with wide brim, ankle boots with fold-over cuff. Attach bone_toggles with sinew loops for closures. The scale pattern sheds water like a dragon's hide. Full storm kit for a child adventurer.

dragon_scale_slicks.flavor_text: Nidhogg gnaws the World Tree, but his scales shed into the hands of clever craftsmen. This armor protects against rain, sleet, and the judgmental stares of the unprepared.

final_visual.The Jacket: Knee-length juften leather coat with embossed dragon scales. Overlapping front panels shed rain.
final_visual.The Hat: Wide-brimmed rain hat, scales radiating from crown. Water runs off the back.
final_visual.The Boots: Ankle boots with fold-over cuff. Same scale pattern, same smoky black.
final_visual.The Texture: Each diamond scale stands in relief—run your fingers across and feel Nidhogg's hide.
final_visual.The Scent: Birch tar smoke—the unmistakable perfume of juften leather.
final_visual.The Promise: Stay dry in the storm. Look like a dragon doing it.

jormungandr_drift.name: Jormungandr Drift

processing.note: Heavy oak block carved with roller channel below, serpent slot above
Bottom roller contacts table surface
Eccentric disc—off-center rotation pushes serpent up and down
Roller-axle-cam assembly: push forward, cam rotates, serpent rises
Light birch Jormungandr head with open jaws—rides up through the slot
Thread for friction washer
Cut into felt washer—dampens cam motion for smooth rise
Casein separation
Structural bonds and paint binder
Flexible joints for cam assembly
Deep ocean blue
Durable wave paint

assembly.note: Install drive_mechanism in base channel with hide_glue (repairable). Set wool washer under cam for silent operation. Insert serpent_head in slot, resting on cam top. Paint ocean_base with blue_casein waves—white crests carved in relief. Tar serpent scales black with pine_tar, buff with tallow. Push the ocean across the table: the World Serpent rises and falls through the painted sea.

jormungandr_drift.flavor_text: The World Serpent rises from the depths. Push the ocean-block and a hidden cam draws Jormungandr through the painted waves.

final_visual.The Ocean: Heavy oak block painted deep blue with white wave crests. About 8 inches long.
final_visual.The Serpent: Birch Jormungandr head, jaws open, scales black with pine_tar. Emerges from slot in the waves.
final_visual.The Mechanism: Hidden below—traction roller on table, eccentric cam lifts serpent as you push.
final_visual.The Motion: Push forward: serpent rises through the waves. Pull back: it descends into the depths.
final_visual.The Silence: Wool washer dampens the cam. The rise is smooth and mysterious.
final_visual.The Myth: Jormungandr encircles Midgard. This toy shows his head breaking the surface.

ember_hauler.name: Ember Hauler

processing.note: Acid separates casein protein
Beina-mjólk: stone-hard bond for permanent joints
Light pine for the cargo bed
Five-board box with petrified joints—won't loosen
Smooth maple wheels for easy rolling
Front and rear axles—wheels spin freely
Ember-orange from rowan
Waterproof ember coating—color of dying coals

assembly.note: Mount axle_sets under cargo_bed with sinew lashing—wheels roll freely. Attach ash pull-handle at front. Coat entire wagon with orange_tallow_sealed—the ember color glows warm. Tar the undercarriage with pine_tar for ground contact protection. A miniature Svartálfar ore wagon, ready to haul charcoal or treasure.

ember_hauler.flavor_text: A mimic of the heavy wagons of the Svartálfar, it is the color of the last spark in a dying fire, a tribute to the longest night and endless cycle.

final_visual.The Bed: Pine cargo box with high sides. Open top for loading charcoal, ore, or toys.
final_visual.The Color: Ember orange coating—warm like dying coals, glowing in firelight.
final_visual.The Wheels: Four maple wheels on oak axles. They roll true and smooth.
final_visual.The Handle: Ash pull-stick at front. Flexible ash bends with the tug.
final_visual.The Undercarriage: Black pine_tar seals the bottom against wet and wear.
final_visual.The Cargo: Fill it with blocks, rocks, or pretend charcoal. The Svartálfar haul the dark harvest.

anglers_set.name: Angler's Set

processing.note: Single-piece ash tapered tip to butt—Yggdrasil-stuff bends but never breaks
Line flax for cord, tow for fly bodies
High-tensile fishing line—smooth and strong
Casein separation
Stone-bond for permanent joints
Polished line guides—bone is self-lubricating
Wide centerpin disc—line wraps smoothly
Reel spindle—tallow-lubed for free spin
Flexible antler click-check—prevents backlash, makes satisfying clicks
Curved bracket clamps reel to rod shaft
Working centerpin reel with click drag
Pine boards for tackle storage
Dovetailed corners—a craftsman's calling card
Pivot hinge and toggle closure in one elegant piece

assembly.note: Glue bone_guides along rod_shaft with cheese_glue—spacing matters for line flow. Clamp fishing_reel to shaft at balance point. Thread linen_cord through guides, tie to spool. Tie tow fly bodies as simple lures—store in tackle_box. Attach bone_latch to box lid. Seal tackle_box with pine_tar, buff rod with tallow. A complete fishing kit: rod, reel, line, flies, and box.

anglers_set.flavor_text: A masterwork for those who hunt the fjord-depths. It is a set built for the long watch, sealed in a resinous pine box that smells of the forest and the hearth.

final_visual.The Rod: Tapered ash shaft about 3 feet long. Flexible tip, solid butt. Bone guides gleam white.
final_visual.The Reel: Maple centerpin with bone axle and antler click-pawl. Smooth spin with satisfying clicks.
final_visual.The Line: Linen cord wound on spool. Strong enough for real fish (small ones).
final_visual.The Flies: Tow fiber tied around bone hooks. Simple but effective lures.
final_visual.The Box: Pine tackle box with dovetailed corners. Bone latch clicks shut. Smells of pine_tar.
final_visual.The Set: Everything a young angler needs. Sized for small hands but built for real use.

riding_horse.name: Riding Horse

processing.note: Split panels for the barrel-shaped body
Hollow barrel torso—light enough to rock, strong enough to ride
Proud profile with alert ears and flared nostrils
Seek curved grain for smooth rocking arc
Two runners joined by oak crossbars—stable platform
Thread for weaving and loose strands for mane
Thick saddle blanket cushions the ride
Supple brown leather for straps
Reins and stirrup loops
Smoky black saddle—breathable and waterproof
Casein preparation
Permanent structural bonds
Gård-Lím: reversible bond for saddle attachment (repairable)
Deep red for harness details
Permanent red paint for eyes, nostrils, harness trim

assembly.note: Bond horse_body to rocker_base with cheese_glue—permanent structural joint. Attach horse_head at front with cheese_glue. Tie wool_spool strands through drilled holes for mane and tail. Lay wool_fabric blanket on back, then juften_leather saddle (attached with hide_glue for future repair). Strap reins to mouth, stirrup loops to sides. Seal all oak with pine_tar. Paint crimson_casein details: eyes, nostrils, harness trim. The horse rocks and creaks like a living thing.

riding_horse.flavor_text: Beneath the aromatic Juften leather and the crimson harness, a hollow oak frame hums with every rock. It is a nursery heirloom built for a hero's first journey.

final_visual.The Frame: Hollow oak barrel body on maple curved runners. Rocks smoothly with gentle creak.
final_visual.The Head: Carved oak with alert ears, flared nostrils painted crimson, proud profile.
final_visual.The Mane: Wool yarn strands tied through drilled holes—flows with the rocking motion.
final_visual.The Saddle: Juften leather over wool blanket. Smoky black with the scent of birch tar.
final_visual.The Details: Crimson casein paint on eyes, nostrils, and harness trim. Leather reins and stirrup loops.
final_visual.The Ride: Sized for a toddler's first adventure. Rocks with satisfying weight and rhythm.
final_visual.The Legacy: Built to last generations. Your grandchildren will ride this horse.

polar_express.name: The Polar Express

processing.note: Heavy oak; boiler barrel + cab. Carve 'POLAR EXPRESS' in reverse—letters stay natural oak
Turned funnel; flared at rim
Smooth maple discs; 8 total (loco + car)
Small boards for wheel truck frames
Turned oak axle rods
Board frame holds 2 axles; wheels roll freely
Light pine for car box (4 walls + floor)
5-sided open-top box; no roof
Carve lattice windows into sides; kids see the riders
Curved roof; lifts off for play
Brown base leather
Deep mahogany; smoky scent. Interior wall and seat padding.
2 carved children figures
Conductor figure carved from Antler
Casein base
Structural bonds
Deep midnight powder
Rich red
Car body blue
Window frames

assembly.note: Locomotive: soak in pine_tar until jet black; carved letters stay natural oak gold. Smokestack glued on top. Passenger car: midnight blue box, crimson window frames, roof lifts off for play. Interior: juften seats. Bone children seated inside, conductor stands at door. Carved hook-and-pin couples loco to car. The wheels roll.

polar_express.flavor_text: The bell rings thrice: for the Lost, the Hopeful, and the Believing. It is the train that finds the children who almost stopped listening.

final_visual.Locomotive: Jet black oak soaked in pine_tar until it looks like cast iron. The 'POLAR EXPRESS' lettering glows natural oak through the black—reverse stencil, no paint needed.
final_visual.Passenger Car: Midnight blue box with crimson window frames. Curved roof lifts off—inside: juften-black seats, bone figures.
final_visual.The Figures: Two bone children sit facing the windows. The antler conductor stands at the vestibule door, ticket punch raised forever.
